extraction.summary: Lists two ways a local-first app loses data, edits kept only in memory and browser eviction, and how to guard against each.

claims.statement: Unsynced edits kept only in JavaScript memory are lost if the tab closes before the next sync.
Request persistent storage once the user has saved real work, and show quota usage so eviction does not come as a surprise.
Even persistent storage can be cleared by the user, so local data still needs a copy outside the browser.

solution.statement: Request persistent storage once the user has saved real work, and show quota usage so eviction does not come as a surprise.

concern.statement: Data in best-effort storage can be evicted by the browser without asking the user when the device runs low on disk space.

solution.statement: The y-indexeddb provider stores a Yjs document in IndexedDB so offline edits survive a page reload.

concern.statement: Unsynced edits kept only in JavaScript memory are lost if the tab closes before the next sync.
